headline: Normal 1Password app lock; broker healthy
summary: 1Password locked at 03:05:34 Eastern on October 20. The broker and keepalive remained healthy. No software repair is warranted; unlocking the app and any required native consent remain Taylor’s actions.
cause: The bounded timestamped log parser found a genuine lock event at 2026-10-20T07:05:34.183+00:00, matching saved keepalive state. This is an app lock, not evidence of a broker crash, stale watchdog or parser failure. The lock trigger is not established. Both last successful account calls occurred at 03:01 Eastern, before the lock, so those historical successes do not establish current authorization.
resolution: No implementation changes, installation, process restart or extra authorization wake were needed. The existing lock suppression is operating as intended. README.md now links this incident and its verified limits; no candidate fix was required.
verification: artifacts/parser-check.json confirms readable logs and agreement with saved lock state without saving raw lines. artifacts/deployed-hashes.json confirms source/deployed worker and keepalive hashes, running keepalive hash, build stamp and codesign validation. artifacts/baseline.json and final-status.json show broker PID/session 1213, /dev/ttys000 and keepalive PID 1214 preserved, heartbeat advancing from 03:06:06 to 03:06:26 Eastern, and unchanged historical account state while locked. artifacts/python-tests.json records 44 passing isolated tests; node-tests.json records 37 passing tests. artifacts/metadata-smoke.json records wrapper --version exit 0 with both output streams discarded; authenticated checks were skipped while locked. artifacts/chat-check.json verifies the exact title, dotfiles directory, Pinned section, strongest advertised supported model gpt-6-astra and high reasoning.
activation: Existing signed service remains running unchanged. Nothing is staged and no next-load activation is required. Unlock 1Password when access is needed and complete native consent if requested; recovery owns the authorization wake.
limitations: Current account authorization was not tested while the app was locked. A successful version check proves wrapper responsiveness, not vault authorization. The reason the app locked and notification click behavior were not tested. No Computer Use or live Claude tests were performed.
docs: Reviewed src/onepassword/README.md, src/onepassword/agent-contract.md and src/onepassword/autofixes/AGENTS.md. Updated README.md with the October 20 incident evidence and authorization limits. The shared contract and autofix guidance already cover this ordinary-lock case; no contract change or sync was needed.
